properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 14 at 2:01PM MDT until September 14 at 2:30PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
SVRGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northeastern Dolores County in southwestern Colorado...
South central San Miguel County in southwestern Colorado...

* Until 230 PM MDT.

* At 200 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 19 miles northwest
of Rico, or 46 miles northwest of Durango, moving east at 30 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage
to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Dunton.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

Torrential rainfall is occurring with this storm, and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 14 at 1:58PM MDT until September 14 at 5:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
FFWABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
West Central McKinley County in west central New Mexico...

* Until 500 PM MDT.

* At 158 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Up to 1.25 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in
the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Gallup, Church Rock, Red Rock State Park, Allison, Gamerco,
Mentmore and Red Rock.

This includes Interstate 40 between Mile Markers 13 and 30.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

In addition to torrential rains, strong winds and hail can also be
expected.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 14 at 1:40PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Tampa Bay Ruskin has issued a
Flood Warning for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Marion, Levy and Citrus
Counties.

.Elevated water levels are expected along the river over the next
several days due to recent heavy rainfall.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...From this afternoon until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 12:45 PM EDT Monday the stage was 28.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage this
afternoon and continue rising to 28.2 feet this afternoon.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.2
feet on 10/02/1979.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at midnight EDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING IN EFFECT FROM THIS AFTERNOON UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued September 14 at 4:15PM EDT until September 14 at 5:45PM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal Waters From  Ochlockonee River to Apalachicola FL out to 20
Nm...
Coastal Waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola out 20 NM...

* Until 545 PM EDT/445 PM CDT/.

* At 414 PM EDT/314 PM CDT/, a strong thunderstorm was located near
St George Island, moving south at 5 knots. The Saint George Island
Bridge weatherstem recently gusted to 33 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots...suddenly higher
waves...frequent lightning...and heavy downpours. Make
sure all on board are wearing life jackets.

* Locations impacted include...
St George Island and Apalachicola.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor immediately as gusty winds and high waves are
expected.
